title: Chapter 1: Honor
brief: The final campaign begins. Commander Yurik leads the proud Dragoon warriors in an invasion of the Akadian homeland to stop General Durand once and for all. For now, the soldiers must contend with the remnants of Durand's fleeing troops.

do.message: Are you ready for this, Commander Yurik?
This will be a difficult task for my Dragoons, Captain Tucker.
For a Dragoon force? You guys are legends. The finest warriors the world has ever seen. You live for the honor of combat.
That is the problem. This is a meaningless diversion, not a suitable enemy.
These troops are outliers of a fearsome enemy force. If we don't deal with them accordingly, we run the risk of endangering our own forces.
Fine. The faster we dispatch these distractions, the more quickly we will be able to stop Durand, and perhaps free his people from their delusions.
You Dragoons are almost surreal. Guaranteed victory against your most bitter enemy, and you're still concerned about the honor of the battlefield.
Soon we will see a return for our people to the homeland. I would not have it tarnished by any manner of shame.
So... I guess you guys are sort of rusty on the whole war thing, right?
Impressive as always, Commander.
I cannot celebrate such an uneven victory. They could never have defeated us.
The closer we get to the Akadian center, the more dangerous this assault will become. I have a feeling Durand isn't out of tricks yet.
My Dragoons have a few surprises for him as well. He has not faced us in a very long time, and we have learned our lessons well.
I'm glad you're on our team, Yurik. To be frank, you can be a pretty intimidating guy.
Thank you. Years of practice.

title: Chapter 2: Arm's Length
brief: The Dragoons occupy a fortified position with the awesome power of their long-range weaponry. Knowing their chances are slim, Durand sends his forces rushing into to assault the Dragoon position while he continues his own retreat.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: Man, I don't know. I expected better from you guys. Seriously.
Again! He cannot call this honorable combat.
I don't think he'd even try. Durand isn't really concerned with all the niceties you seem to practice.
He sends his men to die! Our rockets will destroy them as they beat themselves against the barricades that defend us.
The Akadians are skilled in the mountains. Most importantly, they're hard to hit. It might not be as easy as you think.
But how can they defeat us while we stay behind the barricades. The range of our rockets is immense.
Our rockets can't hit his troops while they are protected by those canyons. Your HUD will show an icon above his units when they are in cover.
I will monitor those icons and try not to be so presumptuous.
You're just going to have to work on some patience for awhile, Yurik.
At last! We must move quickly, men! Durand will slow us down at every turn. We must move swiftly while we can!
Keep your eyes open! Don't forget how dangerous Durand is everyone. We need to keep pushing, but we can't get sloppy.
He has betrayed his people and my own. Started two wars, caused countless deaths. Because of him, my children have never seen the land of my birth.
Sir, the invading forces have breached the borderlands.
Yes. And I'll bet they're feeling very confident. Assured of their victory. We'll let them believe things will be this easy for a bit longer. Then we will teach them what war is.

title: Chapter 3: Air to the Throne
brief: It appears that the Akadians are finally ready to present Command Yurik with the challenge he has been seeking. A squad of aerial and long-range units confront the Dragoons.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: Finally, a battle a warrior can take pride in.
Air forces! Does this mean I'll finally get to see what those toys of yours can do?
The Jammer Truck is no toy, Tucker.
Always serious, huh?
I was raised that way.
The Jammer Truck is a valuable piece of the Dragoon Army's defensive capabilities.
Enemy aircraft will not be able to enter any airspace in the Jammer's range and stealth units will be revealed if they try to travel through it.
Sounds pretty awesome. I guess let's get to this.
Yes. A true battle, at last.
My first chance at a real battle against the Akadians and I have failed. My shame is immeasurable.
Seeing all those planes go down in flames... kind of reminds me of Argent. I hope he's okay.
He is a capable warrior. He will be fine. I am confident he has dispatched Lieutenant Hayne.
I'm not sure I would go that far.
You are not confident in your comrade's abilities?
He's a fine pilot. He's not really very... well... he's just so Argent, you know?
I am afraid I do not know.
Let's just say that there is a lot of whining when he is around.
There is no whining among the Dragoons.
I've noticed.
It's actually in the Constitution.

title: Chapter 4: Arachnaphobia
brief: The Dragoon Army is now firmly within Akadian territory. Trying to make their way through a mountain pass, the Dragoons are met with a series of Akadian barricades meant to slow their progress. A sure sign that an ambush is coming.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: Everyone, be on your guard!
Once we pass these mountains, we will be enclosed within Akadian territory. Retreat will be tricky, if not impossible.
Victory has always been our only option, Captain. This vengeance is our destiny as a people.
Our early scouting parties into this area were all annihilated without broadcasting back any data. There's something here, but we have no idea what.
All that awaits us here is victory over an Akadian enemy. Nothing more.
Have you met Lieutenant Hayne, by chance? He's Akadian, but I get the impression you two might get along.
No one can stand against the spider tank. I love a good ambush.
I hate spider tanks. They give me the willies. Anyone else?
I do not fear anything that I can defeat in battle.
Okay. Guess that's just me then.
Sir. The spider tank outpost has been defeated, sir.
The spider tanks performed admirably. Too bad they were not enough to stop them cold. Prepare the War Machines. Have the spies reported back in?
They have sir. All missions report success.
Excellent. I'm waiting for you Tucker, old friend. Don't take too long...

title: Chapter 5: Bull Horns
brief: Captain Tucker and the Dragoons have come across an Akadian War Machine outpost entrenched in the mountains. They'll have to contend with the War Machines or face constant attacks agains their rear flank as they advance. Supported by rocket trucks, scorpions and spider tanks... these War Machines aren't going to go down easy.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: It's as if this land was built for war.
I know what you mean. Everything's designed to make it hard to get in or out.
There are natural chokepoints everywhere. Assaulting that War Machine could be a strategic nightmare.
It's too bad they don't know that we also have a few tricks up our sleeves.
Would you like to command the Lancers, Tucker?
But those are your secret weapon.
There is no greater thrill than to observe a great weapon wielded with skill. I am curious to see how a man known for his sharp and efficient strikes would make use of a machine like the Lancer.
Remember, Tucker. The penetrating shot of the Lancer's attack will damage two units if they are foolish enough to line themselves up in front of it.
I'll try to make the Dragoons proud.
A fine victory, Tucker. Well done.
Things seem to be going according to battle plans. It makes me nervous. It can't be this easy.
Durand is a coward at heart. He has depended on lies and subterfuge to wreak his havoc. He never would have defeated the Dragoon nation without an unprovoked and surprise invasion.
Then let's keep this convoy moving! We've got a job to do.
Good day, gentlemen. Those Lancers are quite useful.
Durand! Face your judgment.
At your hands? No. I don't think so. No Argent? That's too bad. I guess he wasn't good enough without his pal Tucker to save him all the time. I bet that will weigh on the conscience.
Hayne is surely no match for Federation forces. He was brash and thoughtless, no match for Captain Argent's wit.
And yet, he's not here. Very interesting. I should leave you time to mourn, Tucker. See you soon.
Do not worry, Tucker. He will answer for his crimes, we will see to it. And I am sure your comrade is safe.
I am fairly certain that my young ones back at home, fresh off of the playground, would drive a Lancer better than you have just done, Tucker.

title: Chapter 6: Ghosts
brief: After scouts report that a large radar signature is moving towards the Dragoons via the nearby Khandar River, naval units scramble to deal with a potential assault from the river. What they find is an Akadian assault, but not the kind expected.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: It appears that I may have been wrong about your comrade.
Argent? What do you mean?
Those ships downriver, they are commanded by Lieutenant Hayne. Since he is here and Argent is not, I can only assume that your comrade was defeated.
There has to be some other explanation. Argent is a good soldier... and I'm sure General Pearl would have saved his sorry butt if he got into too much trouble.
Hayne's troops movements are erratic. Indecisive. He is either a brilliant tactician, or...
Tucker! In my way again! And the Dragoons! You're all trying to steal it from me. Well you can't! I'll be the one to kill him. ME! Only me! Victory must be mine. I need to have it.
... totally deranged.
Survey says: bonkers.
Hayne's units are within range. Attack, all units! We must contend with Hayne before we can handle Durand.
Defeated again! I can't get my revenge this way. I must have it, though. I'll find it somewhere else. But where? Where! It's time to go now. Time to vanish.
It's not just me, right? His brain is broken?
It would seem that we are not his final objective. He appears to be after General Durand.
The only thing I can think that would make a loyal soldier turn like that is something that destroys his faith in his commander.
It would seem that your Captain Argent accomplished his mission after all.
He must have shown Hayne the orders we uncovered of Durand calling for secret strikes on Akadian territory. On his own people.
The attacks that started the Dragoon War, the war that drove my people from our homes at the hands of enraged Akadians. All an elaborate lie.
Let's keep moving. I'd like to be very far away from Lieutenant Nutbar before he decides we're in his way again.
Yes! Victory. Durand will be next. Tucker and the Dragoons cannot steal my vengeance from me anymore.

title: Chapter 7: Welcoming Committee
brief: The Dragoon forces will have to ford the Khandar River, which bends to block their advance. Circumventing the river would require crossing the mountains, which the Dragoons cannot do without abandoning all their motorized units. Durand is clearly aware of this barrier and has a contingent of War Machines waiting for the Dragoons on the other side of the the river.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: Welcome esteemed guests! Long time, no see! As you may observe, I have arranged for quite the welcoming committee. Hospitality is important, in spite of our differences.
Be careful. This must be another of Durand's traps. I do not think this is a real welcoming committee.
Do you have sarcasm back home, Yurik?
We must land quickly and prevent our units from being taken in the water. The priority is to secure our War Machine units and the ore deposits needed to fuel them. Move quickly!
I have plenty more gifts waiting for you if you insist on continuing to march to your own deaths.
Your era is done, Durand. We have come to finish things.

Your people will soon know who it was that started the wars that have turned Akadia into a wasteland. When they learn that your power-mongering has led to their downfall, there will be nothing left for you.
If my defeat is so inevitable, then why bother with your fighting? Let the Akadian people police this issue. Why waste more of your lives? Because I assure you, death is coming for you.
Speaking of impending doom, we met Lieutenant Hayne on our way. He was crazed, muttering something about needing to be the one that killed you. Isn't that strange for your vaunted hero?
Lies. Hayne is a loyal Akadian. He would never desert his army.

Funny, I imagine he said the same thing about you right before we showed him your secret orders commanding Akadian troops to fire on their own people, all so you could start a war to pretend to be a hero.
I think I'll kill you first, Tucker.
You can try.
The first sign of a real battle and they crumble. Typical. Now, back to ruling the world...

title: Chapter 8: Argent's Return
brief: True to his word, Durand has another obstacle in store for the Dragoons. As the army advances into a clearing, they are met by a sizable Akadian ambush. Mountains and barricades protect a wide array of Akadian units, presenting a formidable challenge. Unfortunately for Captain Argent, this is exactly when he manages to catch up to his allies.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: Incoming aircraft! It is your comrade Argent.
Argent! Good to see you safe and sound.
*gasp* *pant* Hayne's on his way. *wheeze* He vanished after I showed him the secret orders. He gathered troops to strike Durand and just left. I got here as fast as I could.
Your information is old. Now prepare for the coming assault.

Is he... is this a joke? I'm not going to lie, I'm very out of shape and I did a lot of running to get to this plane, which broke down and I had to fix it with my bare hands. You ever fixed a plane without tools, smart guy?
Sorry, Argent. Hayne showed up already, but we defeated him and he's run off again. As you can see, though, Durand has quite a large ambush waiting for us. So welcome to the party.
Man, I hate you guys.

But hey, for a new chapter in the saga of how much I rule, I put together a new prototype on my journey back. Check out the blue prints for my new flier, the Vulture Drone. I know what you're going to say. I think I'm sexy and intelligent, too.
Durand hides himself again.
He's preparing a final assault. I know him. It's his style.
Good. Soon we will crush Durand and restore our place on this continent.
Peace will be a welcome change.
And then maybe I can take that vacation I keep getting promised.
Yes, then you can exercise some of that flab to be more useful in future ambushes.
Our troops were not strong enough. What did we fail to instill in them? What lessons did we not teach? It does not matter now, though. We can never return home.

title: Chapter 9: The Pass
brief: The main Dragoon force is nearing Durand's central fortress. The assault looks to be nearly impossible, with seemingly endless Akadian forces defending all routes to approach the fortress. Commander Yurik, ever stoic, is ready to advance in the face of insurmountable odds. Lieutenant Hayne, only slightly less unhinged, returns with an alternative for the Dragoon force.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: This is madness.
No. This... is... SP—AR-
Not now Argent.
Oh, come on, man!
We have no choice but to advance. If we retreat now, Durand will have time to regain his power and to escape. We will never be free of him unless we strike.
We'll never be able to breach these defenses. There are simply too many, far more than our scouts had estimated.
Then leave. I do not fear death in the service of my nation.
Don't be too hasty guys. Look who I found lurking outside our base. It's my old buddy!
I wasn't lurking. I came here to help. There is a route. A mountain pass across the lake. It's poorly defended. The terrain there won't support the heavier units. I can take you there.
I don't trust him. I say we ice this greaseball.
Take it easy Argent. I think he's really here to help.
He has to be stopped. I don't... I don't think I can do it alone. I want you to help me. My father died in those strikes on Akadian bases that Durand ordered. I have to help put him to rest.
We move immediately.
You trust him?
You see madness and betrayal behind his eyes, but I see the devotion of a man consumed by his cause. Our vengeance will be his vengeance.
We cannot fail here, Tucker. This battle means too much to our people. If you or Argent do not feel up to the challenge that faces us, I cannot allow you to join us.
We're all ready. Durand has to be stopped.
I dunno. I AM pretty tired.
You don't get a vote.
Father, I will avenge you.
It is settled then. At dawn, we take Durand's fortress. Prepare yourselves.
Oooooh. So close. And yet, so very far away. Maybe next time, team.

title: Chapter 10: Vengeance
brief: Tucker, Yurik and Hayne prepare to assault the last stronghold of General Durand. The General's position is defended with all the units he could muster. It's an impressive force, and the battle looks to be a difficult one, especially since Durand has somehow gotten his hands on a key bit of Dragoon technology.
objective: Do the stuff the brief told you to do... quick... smart...

do.message: We are here.
Hayne's secret pathway did its job. All that's left is the final stronghold for Durand.
We've got to end this.
How is it that you are silent, Argent?
This has been a long time coming for all of us. I'll be able to laugh about this one once it's all over.
Hayne. So it's true? You're a traitor. I did not expect you all so soon, which means he must have led you through our private pathways.
Traitor? Ironic, coming from you.
I never thought I'd have to kill you, Hayne. I almost feel bad about it.
Your time is over, Durand. Today will begin a new era, and the Dragoons will return to our home.
Are you sure about that?
Lancers and Vultures! What the heck?! I just made that like a week ago and you already stole it. Dang, man. That's cold.
My spies are busy little bees. What can I say?
Enough. We're done with your tricks Durand. We're going to put an end to you.
I suppose you think you've won.
Our victory is clear. None of your defenses remain.
In your FACE.
Your people will know what you've done Durand. They'll know they've spent years living in a wasteland due to the aftermath of a war you started. They will never accept you again.
Just execute me if there is nothing left for me.
You will go to prison as punishment for your crimes. Everyone will see what becomes of men like you.
Exactly. As long as I breathe, you will never have won. Never.
Get his sorry butt out of here! I'm tired of hearing him yap. You got schooled, chump! Schooled hard!
Did I miss the whole party?
We did not have a party. Today we had a glorious battle.
No sarcasm.
I always forget they're no good at that. Well, I'm proud of you boys. You did a fine job.

I don't know about you guys, but when I feel proud of someone, I like to shower them with cash. Lots and lots of cash. I'll be right over here when you're ready to start throwing stacks of money at me.
Welcome home, Yurik. It will be nice to have our old neighbors back where they belong.
You have done a brave thing, Tucker. You have risked your life in our cause. This makes us brothers.
Still waiting for my cash shower...
I'm pretty sure there are some Northern Fed parades waiting for you to be Grand Marshall of, Argent? Will you accept fame and an adoring nation instead of cash?
I could be persuaded. Will there be groupies?
Get out of here, all of you! Go! Go be heroes! You've earned it.
Could there have been any other outcome? I hate seeing someone waste their time the way those fools did.
